name: Summer Drought
text: The sun hangs pitiless. Rivers thin to mud and grain curls brown. A drought grips the realm.

choices.label: Pray for rain and dig wells

name: Great Flood
text: Spring thaw bursts the riverbanks. Fields drown and roads wash away under churning water.

name: Earth Tremor
text: The earth heaves. Stone walls crack and a low roar rolls through the valley. Homes shudder.

name: Wildfire
text: A spark in dry timber becomes a wall of flame. Smoke blots the sun as forests burn.

name: Rat Plague
text: Rats swarm the granaries, their chittering a chorus of hunger. Grain sacks empty overnight.

name: Fever Outbreak
text: A burning fever spreads hut to hut. Healers work by candlelight as coughs echo at night.

name: Crop Blight
text: Black spots spread across wheat heads. What looked like bounty rots in the field.

name: Livestock Murrain
text: Cattle drop in pastures, horses stagger. Herders whisper of cursed water.

name: Tax Revolt
text: Collectors return bruised. 'No more!' is chalked on granary doors. The commons refuse the levy.

name: Peasant Uprising
text: Pitchforks catch torchlight. Hungry peasants march on the keep, chanting for bread and justice.

name: Noble Conspiracy
text: Sealed letters pass between manors. Your nobles meet without you, toasting 'a stronger crown'.

name: Clergy Schism
text: Priests preach rival doctrines. Streets divide between old rites and new fervor.

name: Fertile Vein Discovered
text: Surveyors find dark, rich soil beneath scrubland. 'This land will feed generations,' they say.

name: Ancient Ruins Unearthed
text: Ploughs strike dressed stone. A buried vault, its lintel carved with forgotten kings, yawns open.

name: Bumper Harvest
text: Fields bow heavy with golden heads. Even the oldest farmers call it a harvest for the songs.

name: Master Craftsman Arrives
text: A master smith, tools on his back, asks leave to settle. 'Give me a forge and I give you wonders.'

choices.label: Hire and build forge
choices.hint: Costs gold, gains iron and knowledge

name: Traveling Merchant
text: Bells jingle on a caravan. A merchant from distant markets offers exotic goods and news.

name: Royal Marriage Offer
text: A courier bears a silk-sealed letter: a neighboring house seeks union through marriage.

name: Mysterious Stranger
text: A cloaked stranger at the gate claims to know where 'the earth bleeds iron'. Test or trust them?

name: Festival Opportunity
text: The square is ripe for revelry. Musicians gather, asking the crown to bless a festival.

name: Avalanche in the Pass
text: Thunder without storm: snow breaks from the peaks and seals the high pass under white silence.

name: Black Hailstorm
text: Ice stones hammer the fields, shredding young shoots and drumming on thatch.

name: Bitter Frost
text: A frost that cracks timber and stills the millwheel. Breath freezes on beards by dusk.

name: Mill Dam Burst
text: Rotted timbers give way with a crack. The millpond empties through the village lane.

name: Mine Collapse
text: A deep rumble, then dust from the shaft mouth. Timber sets have snapped below.

name: Ashfall from the North
text: Grey snow drifts from a sunless sky. Crops grey over and sheep cough in the fields.

name: Hillside Landslide
text: Rain-loosened earth slides in the night, burying a hamlet's edge under mud and stone.

name: Dust Storm
text: A yellow wall rolls over the plain, scouring fields and filling wells with grit.

name: Lightning Fire
text: Lightning walks the rooftops. A granary roof smoulders, then blooms into flame.

name: River Ice Jam
text: Ice dams the river; black water spreads across low meadows and freezes by night.

name: Bloody Flux
text: Foul water breeds the bloody flux. Sufferers weaken in days; the wells are suspect.

name: Spotted Pox
text: A caravan leaves spotted corpses at the inn. Victims burn then crust; survivors are scarred.

name: Leper Pilgrims
text: Bells ring on the road: white-clad pilgrims seeking the shrine, their faces veiled.

name: Ergot Madness
text: After damp harvest, villagers dance and rave, seeing visions in the rye bread.

name: Sheep Rot
text: Sheep cough and waste on wet pasture. Wool hangs lank; shepherds fear for winter cloth.

name: Child's Cough
text: A whooping cough stalks cradles. Mothers keep night vigil as small chests heave.

name: Year of Fleas
text: Fleas breed in every mattress. Even the hounds bite themselves raw; fever follows bites.

name: Milk Sickness
text: Whole families sicken after drinking new milk. Cows grazed white snakeroot, elders guess.

name: River Flies
text: Black flies cloud the fords, raising weeping sores. Fisherfolk scratch until they bleed.

name: Gaol Fever
text: The dungeon exhales fever. Jailers stagger; prisoners beg air through the grates.

name: Bread Riot
text: Bakers' queues turn to mobs. Loaves are seized; the pillory is toppled into the mud.

name: Serf Flight
text: Whole families slip away by night toward free towns, leaving fields uncut.

name: Guild Strike
text: Hammers fall silent. Guild banners hang from workshops: 'Fair wage or no wares.'

name: Toll Bridge Riot
text: Carters refuse the bridge penny, hurling the toll chest into the river.

name: Apprentice Riot
text: Drunk apprentices smash stalls on holy day, chanting against masters and watch alike.

name: Weavers' Walkout
text: Looms stand empty. Weavers demand wool prices fixed and night work banned.

name: Miners' Sit-In
text: Miners refuse to surface until props are renewed and widows paid. Picks are crossed at the shaft.

name: False Heir
text: A scarred youth claims the old king's blood, and three villages raise his banner.

name: Night Watch Desertion
text: Unpaid watchmen abandon posts, leaving gates to creak unwatched in the dark.

name: Elders' Defiance
text: Village elders bar the reeve from the tithe barn, citing ancient custom and hunger.

name: Silver Lode
text: A shepherd's sling-stone glints wrong. Assayers confirm: silver threads the grey rock.

name: Healing Springs
text: Steam rises from a woodland pool that never freezes. A crippled boy walks home unaided.

name: Kingsleaf Herb
text: Herb-wives find a leaf that staunches fever. Dried bundles sell before they reach market.

name: Starfall Iron
text: Fire crossed the night sky and buried itself in the moor. The metal is sky-hard and strange.

name: Walled Library
text: Masons break into a sealed cellar of scrolls, dry as bone, ink still black as night.

name: Fine Clay Pits
text: Potters praise white clay by the river bend, fit for tiles and fine ware.

name: Wild Herd
text: Dust on the horizon resolves to manes and thunder: a wild herd crops the far meadow.

name: Beehive Valley
text: A valley hums: hollow trees drip honeycomb, and clover runs thick as carpet.

name: Cartographer's Return
text: The lost surveyor staggers home sunburnt, charts of new coasts stuffed in his boots.

name: Glowing Caves
text: Goats vanish into a hill and return dusted with pale light. Caverns of glow-cap mushrooms breathe below.

name: Succession Whispers
text: Courtiers count your coughs and name heirs over wine. The succession is dinner talk.

name: Envoy's Insult
text: A foreign envoy 'mistakes' your throne for a servant's stool and smirks behind his sleeve.

name: Border Treaty
text: Neighbors offer ink and maps: a fixed border, sealed with salt and oath.

name: Council Deadlock
text: Steward and marshal shout past each other; no tax, no levy, no decision by dusk.

name: Spy in the Kitchen
text: A scullion is caught copying seal-marks onto egg-shells. Someone pays for your menus — and more.

name: Rival's Claim
text: A cousin across the mountains stamps your fields onto his coins and calls them his.

name: Tribute Demand
text: A khan's rider demands yearly gold 'for the grass you sit on', twirling his bow.

name: Defector Lord
text: A neighboring lord flees his master with ledgers, horses, and a price on his head.

name: Census Quarrel
text: Counters and reeves brawl over headcounts; villages hide sons in haylofts from the tally.

name: Hostage Exchange
text: Two houses propose swapping sons as pledges of peace, each boy wide-eyed at the gate.

name: Foiled Knife
text: A server's sleeve hides a knife at supper. Guards seize him mid-lunge; he names no master.

name: Chancellor's Graft
text: Ledgers show the chancellor's new roof cost the crown three bridges. Clerks cough politely.

name: Petition of Commons
text: Dusty boots fill the yard: a petition with a hundred thumbprints asks bread, bridge, and school.

name: Old Coronation Debt
text: Moneylenders unroll your father's coronation loans, seals cracked, interest fattened.

name: Market Fire
text: A braziers tips in the night market. Stalls bloom to ash; merchants wail over ledgers.

name: Salt Price Crash
text: New pans flood the market with cheap salt. Housewives rejoice; your salt tithe shrivels.

name: Wool Boom
text: Foreign buyers bid madly for your long wool, silver spilling across counting tables.

name: False Coins
text: Light coins ring false in the market. Someone shaves silver and spends the dust.

name: Guild Monopoly
text: The smiths' guild buys every anvil in town and triples shoeing prices overnight.

name: Toll Windfall
text: Pilgrim season chokes the roads; toll chests overflow with coppers and curses.

name: Iron Shortage
text: Smiths pick over scrap; ploughshares thin and nails are hoarded like silver.

name: Moth in the Wardrobe
text: Moths feast in the cloth stores; fine doublets emerge as lace, unwearable and comic.

name: Great Horse Fair
text: Dealers' tents line the field, manes braided, hooves oiled. The air smells of leather and oats.

name: Timber Rustlers
text: Crown oaks vanish nightly; stumps grin where masts should be. Charcoal pits smoke unlicensed.

name: Grain Speculators
text: Rich men lock full barns while prices climb, waiting for hunger to pay double.

name: Flooded Adit
text: Meltwater drowns the low adit. Ore waits black and gleaming under three feet of cold water.

name: Barge Quarrel
text: Bargemen block the wharf with poled boats, demanding hazard pay for flood season.

name: Surplus Tithe
text: Honest reeves deliver bulging sacks: more than assessed, counted twice and true.

name: Ambush on the Road
text: Arrows from the treeline: a tax wagon overturned, guards bleeding in the ditch.

name: Deserter Band
text: Hungry deserters camp in the woods, stealing chickens and frightening travelers.

name: Border Raid
text: Hooves at midnight, barns ablaze by dawn. Raiders vanish with cattle and captives.

name: Warlord's Challenge
text: A scarred warlord plants his banner on your march and demands single combat of champions.

name: Veterans Return
text: Limping columns come home, banners faded, songs hoarse. They ask only bread and work.

name: Engine Trial
text: Engineers beg to hurl stones at your old wall 'for science'. The wall respectfully disagrees.

name: Recruit Drive
text: Drums and ribbons: sergeants promise glory, boots, and regular meals to farm sons.

name: Hidden Armoury
text: A collapsed chapel disgorges oiled swords of the old wars, wrapped in tarred cloth.

name: Missing Scouts
text: Two riders overdue from the grey hills. Their last pigeon spoke of dust 'like an army'.

name: Rot in the Palisade
text: Mushrooms sprout from the palisade foot; a lean reveals punk-soft heartwood.

name: Free Company Offer
text: A captain of the Ash Company offers two hundred lances, scarred and smiling, for winter coin.

name: Oathbreaker Knight
text: A sworn knight has sold his sword to raiders and knows your patrol paths by heart.

name: Saint's Vision
text: A shepherd girl swears the saint spoke from the oak, bidding wells be cleaned and debts forgiven.

name: Heretic Preacher
text: A barefoot preacher calls priests fat and tithes theft. Crowds grow daily at the crossroads.

name: Relic Procession
text: The finger-bone of St. Aldric tours the villages; the lame queue and the innkeepers grin.

name: Monastery Fire
text: Candles or malice — the scriptorium burns. Monks hurl books from windows into snow.

name: Tithe Dispute
text: Abbot and reeve both claim the same sheaves; farmers watch, scythes in hand, to see who blinks.

name: Pilgrim Flood
text: Thousands tramp the shrine road, singing, begging bread, dropping coins and fever alike.

name: Darkened Sun
text: Midday dims to dusk; birds hush. The crowd falls to knees, certain the heavens judge them.

name: Weeping Statue
text: The Virgin weeps — water, wine, or miracle? Queues form before dawn either way.

name: Bishop's Warning
text: The bishop's letter is read aloud: amend the chapel tax or face exclusion from holy rites.

name: Choir School
text: Choirmaster begs coin for boys' voices to be trained 'to crack heaven's plaster'.

name: The Ruler's Dream
text: Three nights the same dream: a crown of blackbirds dissolving into grain. The court waits for meaning.

name: Queen's Garden
text: The queen begs a walled garden of roses and simples, 'a green peace against stone quarrels'.

name: Heir's Fever
text: The little heir burns and babbles; physicians bleed, nurses pray, the realm holds breath.

name: Royal Hunt
text: Stags fatten in the royal forest; huntsmen bay for the horn and the court's favor.

name: Jester's Satire
text: The fool mimes your council — hunchbacked, snoring, pockets out — and the hall roars helplessly.

name: Old Friend Returns
text: A scarred companion of youth waits at the gate, grinning gap-toothed, asking a place — any place.

name: Bitter Cup
text: Your wine tastes of bitter almonds; the taster sleeps and does not wake by supper's end.

name: Royal Portrait
text: A painter from the south begs sittings, promising immortality 'in lapis and egg'.

name: Sleepless Nights
text: You walk the battlements at third bell, counting stars and debts while the castle sleeps.

name: Bastard Rumor
text: Taverns sing of a miller's child with your eyes. The queen does not sing.
